loan.title: The loan
loan.desc: What you borrowed and on what terms.

loan.annuityHint: Same payment every month. Most common.
loan.serialHint: Same principal every month, so payments start high and fall.
loan.startHint: Shows where you are today on the graph.
loan.remainingHintWithStart: From your latest statement. Leave empty to estimate from the plan.
loan.estimateSerial: Roughly <0>{{amount}}</0> per month at the start.
loan.moreHint: start date, balance, fees, day count
loan.rateHint: The floating (nominal) rate, not the effective rate.
loan.feeHint: The fee on each bill (termingebyr). On your invoice or loan agreement, often 0–75 kr.
loan.setupFeeHint: One-off fee when the loan was taken out. Include the registration fee (tinglysingsgebyr) if the bank counts it in the effective rate.
loan.bankEffectiveHint: From the bank. Optional, used to check the fees.
loan.effHigher: The bank says {{bank}} %. The gap is usually fees that are missing, most often the monthly fee.
loan.effLower: The bank says a lower {{bank}} %. Check the rate, the term, the fees, and whether the loan starts interest-only or interest-free.
loan.effSolve: Find the monthly fee that gives {{bank}} %
loan.effNoSolve: No fee between 0 and 10 000 kr gives {{bank}} %. Check the other numbers.
loan.effAbout: The effective rate includes monthly compounding and all fees. Interest itself is always charged at the nominal rate.
loan.introHint: Common on many loans, for example the first 3 years interest-only or at 0 %. Counted as part of the loan.
loan.effUnusual: That would take a monthly fee of {{fee}}, which is unusually high. The amount, term, setup fee or start terms probably differ from what the bank used.
loan.dayCountHint: It's in the loan terms. Floating-rate loans usually use actual days (365/365). 365/360 costs a little more.

extras.title: Pay extra
extras.desc: Every krone goes straight to the principal.
extras.empty: Nothing yet. Try 1 000 kr a month and watch the years fall off.

periods.desc: Months that differ from the normal plan: only paying interest when money is tight, or a different rate such as 0 % or a fixed-rate deal.
periods.empty: No periods yet. Add one to see what a few interest-only months, or a 0 % deal, really does.
periods.rateHint: The payment is recalculated for this rate, and again when the period ends.

verdict.noChanges: Use "What if …?" to see what extra payments, interest-only months or another rate do to the loan.
verdict.planSoFar: The plan as it stands: paid off in {{duration}}, costing <0>{{amount}}</0> in interest and fees.
verdict.noEffect: Your changes don't affect the loan
verdict.paidOffBody: Given the start date and remaining balance there is nothing left to pay.
verdict.truncated: The plan stops after 100 years. This doesn't add up, shorten the pauses.

loans.title: My loans
loans.privacyBody: Nothing you type about your loans is collected or sent anywhere. Loans are stored only in this browser's local storage. We only count anonymous visits, without cookies and without any loan data. Clearing site data removes your loans, so use <0>Export</0> to keep a backup or move between devices.

loans.deleteAllDesc: This removes every saved loan from this browser. There is no undo, so export first if in doubt.
loans.deleteOneDesc: Removes this loan from the browser. No undo.

timing.outside: This is outside the loan's lifetime, so it has no effect.

scan.title: Fill in from a screenshot
scan.desc: Take screenshots of the loan details in your online bank. The app reads the text and suggests values for you to check.
scan.drop: Drop screenshots here, or paste with ⌘V / Ctrl+V.
scan.tip: The loan details page works best. Several images can be read at once.
scan.error: Couldn't read the image. Try again, or fill in by hand.
scan.nothing: No loan details found. Try a screenshot of the loan details page.
scan.review: Here's what was found. Untick anything that's wrong.
scan.privacy: Images are read in your browser and never uploaded.
scan.derivedDueDay: Moved to the due day ({{day}}) so payments land on the right day
scan.derivedEndDate: Worked out from the start and end dates
scan.derivedFee: Worked out: payment minus principal and interest

help.name: A name so you recognise the loan, for example "DNB mortgage". Only you see it.
help.category: Pick what kind of loan it is, and the app suggests usual values and a typical rate right now.
help.amount: The amount you originally borrowed. It's in the loan agreement or your online bank as "original loan amount". If you don't have it, use today's balance.
help.rate: The rate the bank charges, also called the nominal or floating rate. It's in your online bank. Don't use the effective rate here.
help.effective: The effective rate is the nominal rate plus fees, expressed as one yearly percentage. The bank states it. Fill it in to check that your fees add up.
help.term: How long the loan runs in total, from start to the last payment. It's in the loan agreement. Mortgages are often 25–30 years, car loans 5–7.
help.type: Annuity: the same amount every month, mostly interest at first. Serial: equal principal payments, so the payment starts high and falls. Most mortgages are annuity loans.
help.intro: Some loans start with interest-only years, where you pay only interest, or interest-free years at 0 %. It's in the loan agreement.
help.startDate: The date the loan started. Pick the same day of the month as you pay, so payments land on the right day. Used to show how far you've come.
help.remaining: How much you owe today. It's in your online bank as "balance" or "current loan amount". Leave it empty to work it out from the plan.
help.fee: The fee added to every bill. It's on your invoice or in the loan agreement, often 0–100 kr.
help.setupFee: The one-off fee when the loan was set up, often plus a registration fee. It only affects total cost and the effective rate.
help.dayCount: How the bank counts interest days. Most floating-rate loans use actual days (365/365). It's in the loan terms. If unsure, leave it.
help.extras: An extra payment that goes straight to the debt. Your payment stays the same, but the loan ends sooner and you pay less interest.
help.goal: Pick when you want to be done, and the app works out how much extra you need to pay each month, or as one lump sum.
help.periods: Periods that differ from the plan: interest-only, where you pay just interest, or another rate, such as 0 % or a fixed-rate period.
help.after: After an interest-only period the bank either keeps the end date, so the payment goes up, or keeps the payment, so the loan runs longer.

insight.split: Of your next payment of {{payment}}, {{interest}} goes to interest, {{principal}} to principal and {{fee}} to fees.
insight.interestOnly: Your next payment of {{payment}} is interest only ({{interest}}) plus fees. The debt doesn't go down in this period.
insight.turn: From {{date}}, more goes to principal than to interest.
insight.stressHint: Pick how many percentage points to see what it means for you.
insight.stressResult: At {{rate}} % the payment becomes {{payment}}, {{delta}} more a month. The loan costs {{cost}} more in total.

compare.title: Compare
compare.desc: Compare two loan offers, or check whether moving your loan to another bank pays off.
compare.verdict: {{name}} is {{total}} cheaper in total, and {{monthly}} less a month at first.
compare.same: The offers cost the same in total.
compare.todayDesc: From the calculator. Change the loan there to update.
compare.switchCostHelp: The new bank's setup fee plus the registration fee (tinglysing), and any fee for paying off the current loan. Often 1 500–4 000 kr.
compare.newTermHint: Same as today: {{term}}. A longer term lowers the payment but often costs more overall.
compare.switchYes: Switching saves you {{total}} in total. The switching cost is earned back after {{months}} months ({{date}}).
compare.switchNo: Switching doesn't pay off: it costs {{total}} more in total.
compare.useNew: Open the new loan in the calculator
compare.needLoan: Fill in your loan in the calculator first, then you can check whether switching pays off.
